I’m 52 this year, and I’ve farmed this land in Quzhou for 30 years, so I mostly go by what has worked on my own fields and what I see nearby. I have only 10.1 mu, so I can’t gamble too much. My main land is still wheat-maize, because that gives steadier grain and spreads the risk. This year I’ll keep about 7 mu in wheat-maize rotation and put 3.1 mu into potato. The wheat is already in the ground from last autumn, so at the start of this season my main decisions are how much topdressing and irrigation to give it, then how fast I turn that land over into summer maize after harvest. I have well water, but pumping costs money, so I won’t irrigate just because I can. Usually I give wheat the key water at jointing and heading if the soil is dry, and maize maybe once or twice depending on rain. The extension guy says don’t overdo nitrogen, but in our place if wheat looks pale and I hold back too much, yield can fall fast, so I still keep rates a bit on the safe side.

For potato, I won’t make it too big because it needs more hands and more care, and some people in my family work off-farm. Potato can bring cash, but seed and pesticide cost more, and if disease comes it is troublesome. So I keep it on a smaller patch that the family can manage. I’ll use round numbers, not fancy calculation: enough base fertilizer to make sure the crop stands, then one follow-up for wheat and maize if the crop looks like it needs it. I’d rather keep some cash in hand than push every mu to the limit.
